podcast.title: "Domino-style Piano" on I Hear You Knockin' (1955)
podcast.body: Huey Piano Smith played a distinctive "very fat, Domino-style piano" on Smiley Lewis's 1955 hit "I Hear You Knockin'," an arrangement credited to Dave Bartholomew that showcased a common New Orleans R&B bass line. "featuring Huey Piano Smith playing a very fat, domino-style piano domino."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Early Rock and Roll Piano Hero
podcast.body: Huey Piano Smith was an early pioneer of rock and roll, recognized as one of the "piano heroes" who shaped the genre's sound during its nascent stages. His energetic piano work contributed significantly to the "honkin rhythm" that was a hallmark of early rock and roll. "Instead, the early pioneers were piano heroes, Little Richard, Jerry Lee Lewis, Fats Domino, Ray Charles, Huey Piano Smith."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: New Orleans Piano Player
podcast.body: Huey "Piano" Smith was one of two great New Orleans piano players brought in for Little Richard's first Specialty Records session. He played in the same style as Fats Domino and was a veteran of sessions for Domino or artists who worked in Domino's style. "Blackwell also brought in two great New Orleans piano players, Huey, Piano Smith and James Booker, both of whom were players in the same style as Domino."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

xref.title: Early Rock and Roll Piano Hero
xref.body: Little Richard was an early pioneer of rock and roll, recognized as one of the "piano heroes" who led the genre before the electric guitar became dominant. These pioneers were known for their energetic piano playing, contributing to the "honkin rhythm" that characterized early rock and roll, which evolved from rhythm and blues combos. "Instead, the early pioneers were piano heroes, Little Richard, Jerry Lee Lewis, Fats Domino, Ray Charles, Huey Piano Smith."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Rock and Roll Piano Hero
xref.body: Jerry Lee Lewis was a foundational pioneer of rock and roll, counted among the "piano heroes" whose piano playing was central to the genre's initial sound. His style was key in shaping the percussive and energetic rhythm and blues-influenced foundation of early rock. "Instead, the early pioneers were piano heroes, Little Richard, Jerry Lee Lewis, Fats Domino, Ray Charles, Huey Piano Smith."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Rock and Roll Piano Hero
xref.body: Fats Domino was an early pioneer in rock and roll, identified as one of the "piano heroes" whose instrument was fundamental to the genre's formation. His contributions helped integrate elements of jazz, boogie-woogie, and barrel house into the emerging rock sound. "Instead, the early pioneers were piano heroes, Little Richard, Jerry Lee Lewis, Fats Domino, Ray Charles, Huey Piano Smith."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Rock and Roll Piano Hero
xref.body: Ray Charles was an early pioneer of rock and roll, considered one of the "piano heroes" who helped define the genre in its formative years. His piano style was instrumental in blending various musical influences, including jazz and rhythm and blues, into rock and roll. "Instead, the early pioneers were piano heroes, Little Richard, Jerry Lee Lewis, Fats Domino, Ray Charles, Huey Piano Smith."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
